### <ins> Week 1 HW </ins>                                                 Find 3-5 datasets/data sources that are relevant to your interests. Provide a brief summary of each of the datasets. Describe why the dataset is interesting to you / how it relates to your interests. Hypothesize, in general terms, how you might use code to sort / structure / filter the dataset. General Interests/Topics for Assignment:                                                
**[MOMA Data source]:** (https://github.com/museumofmodernart/collection)
-    The MOMA collection dataset is an ongoing data collection of various forms of art,  spanning over 200,000 works. The data collection has some incomplete information, especially since the GitHub repository is continuously being updated. However, it has information such as date acquired, artist, title, etc.  
  The dataset interests me because I would really like the opportunity to work with museum data. One of the things that drew me not only to this class, but to Pratt Overall, was how to incorporate data management into cultural institutions. I worked in an art museum during my undergrad, which sparked my interest in working with museum data and the possibility of pursuing it long term.
  First and foremost, I would filter the data by year. I would use a range to help filter through thousands of data entries, such as the entire 80s. They did an exhibit a few years ago that highlighted 80s artwork, and I really enjoyed it. I would filter the data by gender and, if possible, by type of artwork such as film and design. I would use code to try to sort the type of artwork in this period that had the most submissions or sort it by theme. As I investigate further, I wonder whether there is data on museum engagement by exhibit type, artwork, or artist highlight.

**[NYC Parks Property]**:  (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Recreation/Parks-Properties/enfh-gkve/about_data)

-    The NYC Parks Properties dataset from NYC Open Data analyzes park properties managed by NYC Parks. The data collection highlights data such as the borough the park is located in, agencies that manage the park, proximity to waterfront, etc. The dataset is interesting to me because I have spent the last few months working in a park and helping assist with free events held in the park. This brought to my attention the amount of work that goes into upkeep, but also when I came across this in NYC open data, I thought it would be so cool to analyze all of the parks in NYC. What makes them desirable for visitors, and what resources they have that would benefit visitors as well. 
    I would sort this data by borough first. It would be interesting to see the total number of parks managed by NYC Parks in each borough. Then, I would sort the data by proximity to bodies of water and proximity to police precincts. It would be interesting to see how the proximity to those will alter foot traffic in either of these parks. As I investigate further, I would like to analyze the foot traffice based on these logisitics and could be useful for parks to analyze to help with more visitor engagement.


**[US transportation and Health]:** (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/us-state-transportation-health) 

-    This dataset analyzes the relationship between transportation modes and health status in each state. The dataset has columns for different modes of transportation, travel miles, physical activity, and proximity to major highways. This dataset is really interesting to me because I’ve always wanted to work with transportation data, and it would be interesting to analyze a state like NY vs a state in the Midwest and how the different modes of transportation are benefiting or harming their population. 
   I would sort the data by each mode of transportation and analyze the physical activity and miles traveled for each one individually first. Then I would combine it to draw comparisons between the transportation modes. It would also be interesting to analyze what the most common health issues are aligned with each mode. 

**[Traveler Trip Dataset]:** (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/rkiattisak/traveler-trip-data)
-   This dataset analyzes flight logistics from destination to traveler demographics to observe travel patterns. This dataset is interesting because it would be cool to see the travel patterns that come to light depending on which variable is highlighted. I would sort this data by duration and destination to see what patterns arise. Then I would sort the data by demographics such as gender to see which demographic tends to travel the farthest and to what country.
